items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: It was run by a very, very nice man called Ralph Watkins. And some years later, after I left Calvin, he hired me to play the Embers in New York

ctx.x: You’re the first person I told this story to I think. So I didn’t get it, and I’m glad I didn’t. Because it would take me away again, and I was concentrating on getting my own thing going eventually. I got a job with a man called Calvin Jackson. He was a brilliant pianist. He was the assistant musical director at MGM with Johnny Green. Brilliant musician. And he had this job, at a very nice sophisticated hotel in Toronto, and a weekly radio series and a weekly television series. And he hired me to be a guest on…

the critic for the Global Mail, a music critic, which is one of our big papers up there. And he played clarinet. So at the end of the concert he said, “Do you know Goodman?” I said, No I don’t know him, he’d never remember me,” I said, “He came to see me one night twelve years ago.” He said, “Well let’s go backstage and see if we can get a few words from him.” I said, “Okay.” So we go back and the dressing room door is open. And here’s Benny sitting with a bottle of a Mickey, a black and white whiskey, a Scotch…
